svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 2. The two states your phone can be in when somebody else is holding it
svg.desc: A state diagram. Before first unlock, the keys protecting most user data have not been derived and the data stays sealed, which current extraction tools largely cannot get past. After the first unlock, keys are resident in memory and far more is reachable, and this is the state a phone is in almost all of the time. One unlock moves the device from the first state to the second, and only a power off or a reboot moves it back. Current iPhone software performs that reboot automatically after seventy two hours without a successful unlock, managed by the secure processor. Three actions follow: powering the device off deliberately, understanding that passcodes and biometrics are treated differently by courts, and enabling Lockdown Mode where the threat justifies it.
svg.text: The most likely serious thing that happens to a phone, and the part of mobile privacy that platform comparisons never cover.

g.text: The keys protecting most user data have not
been derived yet, so the data stays sealed.
Current extraction tooling largely cannot
get past this state.
Some system data and a few cached fragments remain.

svg.text: unlocked at least once since it last booted

g.text: Keys are resident in memory. Far more of the
device is reachable by somebody holding it.
This is the state your phone is in almost
every waking moment of every day.
Locking the screen does not leave this state.

svg.text: Only a power off or a reboot returns it. Current iPhone software does this automatically after 72 hours without a successful unlock,
managed by the secure processor, and it is not defeated by airplane mode, shielding, or keeping the device on a charger.

g.text: The entire control, and it takes three
seconds. Power off before a border, a
protest, a search, or anywhere you
expect the phone to leave your hand.
Locking the screen is not this.
A locked phone that was unlocked this
morning is still in the right hand box.
Learn the shortcut on your device now,
so you can do it without looking, in a
pocket, under stress.
A face or a fingerprint is convenient
and can be applied to you while you
are holding still.
In the United States courts treat a
passcode as protected speech, and are
split on whether a biometric is.
One federal appeals court said in 2024
a fingerprint may be compelled; another
said in 2025 it may not. Unresolved.
Learn how to disable biometrics fast.
A built in hardening setting that turns
off features known to carry targeted
spyware. It costs you some conveniences
and nothing else.
The vendor stated in March 2026 that it
knows of no successful mercenary spyware
attack against a device with it enabled.
Four years, against the best funded
attackers there are. That is a rare claim
and it has held up.

svg.text: Why this figure exists, and why it is not in the material it replaces
A guide that spends thirty minutes on advertising identifiers and none on this has ranked the threats by how much is written about them rather than by how likely
they are. You are far more likely to lose a phone, or hand one over at a checkpoint, than to be individually targeted by an advertising network.
Every control on this page is free, takes minutes, and works the same on both platforms. Do these before you change a single privacy toggle.
